ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, and the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person (PEP) as defined under FATF Recommendations, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs. Continuous monitoring and periodic re-screening must occur at least annually and upon any trigger event such as a change in ownership or adverse media. All screening results must be documented, risk-rated, and retained for at least five years. For the scrap copper trading sector, additional checks against the Basel AML Index and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public statements are mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Online Registry (i-REG)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul). Foreign names may be transliterated phonetically into Hangul. The name must consist of a unique corporate designation (e.g., 'Yuhan Hoesa' for LLC) followed by a business purpose. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Four-tier naming conventions: (1) uniqueness, (2) no prohibited words, (3) no misleading terms, (4) compliance with the Commercial Act.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: New England City and Town Area

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Third Book, Chapters IV and V, Articles 543 through 632, together with the Supreme Court Registration of Commercial Entities Rules and the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources for ancillary licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, accessible through the Korean Court Internet Registration Service (Ireg)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Registration / Corporation Registration Application and the associated Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a Yuhan Hoesa under current Korean law; the Articles of Incorporation must state the subscribed capital but there is no statutory minimum or mandatory blocked escrow account. However, 100 percent of the subscribed capital contributions must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company or the promoter prior to registration, and no withdrawal from that account is permitted before the district court registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS / MANAGING MEMBERS OF YUHAN HOESA

WHEREAS, the Members and Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, have caused the Articles of Incorporation to be signed and subscribed for the purpose of carrying out cross-border physical consignment, trading, sorting, and logistics coordination of shredded non-ferrous copper scrap and other residual metal compounds;

WHEREAS, all statutory formation requirements have been fulfilled, including payment of capital contributions, reservation of the corporate name, and preparation of the registered office;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED as follows:

1. Ratification of Incorporation. The incorporation of the Company and the actions of the founding members in subscribing to the Company's stated capital, opening the initial bank account, and retaining legal counsel are ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects.

2. Registered Office and Service Point. The board adopts and confirms the principal office at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation as the Registered Office. The Registered Office shall be the legal seat, the place of statutory meeting, and the official address for receipt of judicial and administrative process.

3. Banking and Treasury Authorization. The board authorizes the representative director, together with one other designated director or corporate secretary, to execute account documentation, sign documentary letters of credit, and operate Swift TT payment rails. All bank instructions shall require two authorized signatories and shall be documented in the corporate financial register.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The board appoints the representative director, one internal auditor or compliance officer, and one corporate secretary as statutory officers to maintain the corporate registry, board minutes, member ledger, tax records, and environmental compliance files.

5. Regulatory Filings. The board delegates to the statutory officers full authority to prepare and submit all applications under the Wastes Control Act, the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources, the Commercial Act, and relevant tax laws, including the waste recycling business report, transboundary movement permits, export clearance filings, and all environmental approvals.

6. Effectiveness. This resolution is effective upon adoption and remains in force until amended or rescinded by a subsequent resolution.

RESOLVED, that the statutory officers are directed to file a certified copy of this resolution in the corporate records and to take any further lawful acts necessary to implement these authorizations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Corporate Name and Prepare Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Court Internet Registration Service (Ireg) / Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant shall file an online corporate name reservation through Ireg using the exact proposed name Yuhan Hoesa. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered Korean entity. Concurrently, the founding members shall prepare and execute the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, business purpose, total subscribed capital, member contributions, registered office address, director appointment provisions, and duration. If any foreign member executes the articles, the member's signature must be authenticated by apostille and the articles shall be accompanied by a certified Korean translation. The name reservation is valid for thirty days and must be cited in the later court filing.
required_dossiers: Online corporate name reservation application
Passport or national identification card of each founding member
Apostilled certificate of identity or residence for foreign members
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney to the local incorporation agent
Lease agreement or utility bill evidencing the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to similarity or prohibited words, the applicant shall revise the Articles of Incorporation by choosing a secondary candidate and resubmit the reservation within the statutory two-month response period. If the court informally rejects the articles, amend the contested clauses and resubmit through Ireg with supplemental explanations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Subscribed Capital into a Designated Korean Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service-authorized commercial bank such as Shinhan, Woori, KB Kookmin, Hana, or equivalent, acting through the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director shall open a temporary corporate capital deposit account in the name of the Yuhan Hoesa or of the promoter as permitted by banking practice. Each member must remit or deposit the full amount of their subscribed contribution, and the bank shall issue a certificate of paid-in capital deposit. No statutory escrow account is mandatory, but the deposit certificate must be presented to the district court registrar. The funds may not be withdrawn before registration is completed. After registration, the account shall be converted into the company's operating account and its signatories shall be aligned with the board resolution.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation certificate
Apostilled identification documents of the representative director
Articles of Incorporation
Bank account opening application
Capital contribution schedule and remitter source of funds
Beneficial ownership disclosure and anti-money laundering questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide audited financial statements, bank statements, or a certificate of source of wealth. If the deposit is rejected and returned, re-deposit the funds under instruction from the corporate service provider and obtain a fresh certificate of paid-in capital deposit before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office (via Ireg electronic filing or in-person counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director shall submit the incorporation registration application to the competent district court registrar. The registrar will verify the Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, name reservation, registered office evidence, and directors' written acceptance of office. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the registrar will register the members, capital, statutory officers, and registered office. Upon approval, the court issues the certificate of corporate registration. The registration must be completed within the period specified in the Commercial Act after the date of subscription unless a judicial extension is obtained. The applicant must also pay the stamp and registration fee and preserve the receipt in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation registration application form
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued by the bank
Certificate of corporate name reservation
Written acceptance of office signed by each director
Evidence of registered office, including lease contract or certificate of title
Copy of the representative director's registered seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction or supplementation order, the applicant shall cure the defect, pay any supplementation fee, and resubmit within the registrar's prescribed period, usually fourteen days. If the registration is suspended for identity verification, submit apostilled original documents and a certified Korean translation together with a petition for expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Business with the National Tax Service and Open the Operating Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Tax Service (NTS) tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office, and the selected commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after issuance of the court certificate of incorporation registration, the company shall file a business registration application through the HomeTax online portal or at the local NTS office. The application must identify the corporate income, value-added tax, and withholding tax accounts. Upon approval, the NTS issues the business registration certificate, which must be displayed at the registered office. The company shall then present the court registration certificate, NTS business registration certificate, and board resolution to the bank to convert the temporary capital account into the operating account, open a corporate current account, and execute the two-signatory mandate for documentary LC and Swift TT transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration from the district court
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Representative director's identification and seal certificate
Lease contract or certificate of ownership for the registered office
Corporate bank account application and corporate seal
Entity and signatory anti-money laundering and know-your-client forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the registered office as non-commercial, provide a building occupancy certificate and zoning compliance letter. If the bank declines the account opening due to AML concerns, submit a corrected beneficial ownership declaration, board resolution, and notarized source-of-funds statement, or apply to a second-tier commercial bank with the same dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Waste Recycling Business Report, Transboundary Movement Approval, and Export License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment (MoE), Korea Environment Corporation, local Metropolitan/Provincial Government waste management department, and Korea Customs Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the company will physically trade, sort, and consign shredded non-ferrous copper scrap, it must file a waste recycling business report with the competent local government. The report must describe the scrap storage facility, weighing equipment, sorting lines, fire safety systems, and environmental controls. If scrap is exported abroad, the company must also obtain transboundary movement approval under the Wastes Control Act and comply with the Basel Convention and OECD Council Decision. The applicant shall submit the corporate registration certificate, storage facility lease or ownership proof, fire safety certificate, scale calibration certificate, export contracts, and a material flow plan. After the local government approves the report, the company must register with Korea Customs Service as an exporter and obtain any trade statistics code for non-ferrous waste metal.
required_dossiers: Waste recycling business report form
Certificate of corporate registration
Proof of ownership or valid lease of the scrap storage yard
Firefighting facility maintenance and inspection certificate
Scale calibration certificate issued by an authorized metrology agency
Material flow diagram for copper scrap sorting and weighing
Copy of the export sales contract and destination recovery certificate
Environmental registration or exemption certificate for the facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the waste recycling report is returned for supplementary correction, the applicant shall correct the facility diagram, add missing fire prevention equipment, and resubmit within the statutory grace period. If the report is denied, the company may file an administrative appeal with the Metropolitan/Provincial Governor under the Administrative Appeals Act, and thereafter may bring an administrative suit to the competent district court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Environment (MoE); Korea Environment Corporation; local Metropolitan/Provincial Government waste management department; Korea Customs Service for export authorization
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Waste Recycling Business Report Confirmation Certificate and Transboundary Waste Movement Approval Certificate for shredded non-ferrous scrap

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment - Environmental Justice and Impact Assessment Division; Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Environmental Registration for a non-hazardous waste recycling and trading operation. A Full Environmental Impact Assessment or Prior Environmental Review will be triggered only if the operation constructs or operates a sorting or warehouse facility with total floor area exceeding 10,000 square meters, or if the site is located within an environmentally protected area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges from stockpile runoff must comply with Korean Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards: BOD no greater than 40 mg/L, COD no greater than 40 mg/L, suspended solids no greater than 40 mg/L, total nitrogen no greater than 60 mg/L, and total phosphorus no greater than 8 mg/L. Stormwater runoff must maintain oil and grease concentration no greater than 15 mg/L. Fugitive dust at the facility boundary shall not exceed 0.5 mg/m3. No volatile organic compound emissions are expected from clean copper scrap; if insulation or coatings are present, the contaminated fraction must be containerized and tested under the Korean Standard Leaching Test with thresholds of Cu 3 mg/L, Pb 3 mg/L, Cd 0.3 mg/L, and Cr6+ 1.5 mg/L before disposal or recovery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate approved by the National Fire Agency, including automatic fire detection, portable extinguishers, fire water supplies, and compliance with National Fire Safety Code 101 for warehouses; structural load inspection certificate issued by an authorized structural engineer for scrap stacking and rack stability; and workplace safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act administered by the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, covering dust control, noise exposure limits, manual handling procedures, emergency evacuation, and personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), headquartered in Seoul, acting through local district tax offices and the electronic HomeTax portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr), with customs and foreign-trade data consigned through the Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNIPASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC: after registration of the company under the Commercial Act, the LLC must file a statutory business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its principal place of business. The application must be accompanied by the certificate of corporate registration, articles of incorporation, director identification, and evidence of the registered business address. The NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the unified Tax Identification Number and VAT registration identifier used on tax invoices. For a foreign non-resident entity that has neither incorporation nor a permanent establishment in Korea but performs VAT-taxable transactions in Korea, registration is effected through a resident tax representative: the representative files the non-resident business registration application with NTS together with a power of attorney, the foreign certificate of incorporation/business license, translation, and banker's reference evidencing the non-resident's identity. Where the non-resident has a fixed place of business in Korea, registration is completed through that place of business and any foreign branch must also register before issuing tax invoices. Registration must be completed before taxable supplies commence; late registration attracts procedural penalty assessments and suspends the issuance of legally effective e-invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate a check-the-box entity-classification election. A domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC is subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT as a separate juridical person; there are no elective pass-through classification regimes analogous to the United States. Hybrid mismatch treatment is controlled by mandatory anti-hybrid rules in the Framework Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and no voluntary election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is mandatory from commencement of business; no general annual turnover threshold exempts a business from registration. A simplified taxpayer with prior-year taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000 may use the simplified VAT computation regime, but registration and electronic tax-invoice compliance remain statutory. For non-resident suppliers of Korean taxable supplies, registration is obligatory when taxable turnover begins, with no minimum exemption threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are compulsory under Article 32 of the Value Added Tax Act. Every VAT-registered entrepreneur that issues a tax invoice must transmit it electronically through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax-invoice operation (including licensed EDI software vendors), which assigns a unique electronic invoice number and stores it in the NTS database. There is no per-transaction government fiscal stamping, but the system is designed for real-time or near-real-time transmission, automated matching, and anti-fraud verification; the NTS cross-checks issued e-invoices against the recipient's business registration number, VAT returns, customs declarations, and foreign exchange records, and failure to transmit within the statutory electronic transmission period results in penalty surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value Added Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated. To claim the 0% export VAT rate for recycled scrap copper wire, the following statutory criteria must be met: (1) the goods must be physically exported from South Korea under a customs export declaration accepted by KCS; (2) the export contract and commercial invoice must be in the name of the Yuhan Hoesa LLC or, if handled through a trade intermediary, the actual exporter must be identifiable and the proof of export must correspond with the VAT-taxable person; (3) the goods must leave Korea within a reasonable period and the customs export manifest must identify the foreign buyer's destination; and (4) the export proceeds must be received from a non-Korean purchaser through a Korean won or foreign-currency bank settlement in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For physical goods, zero-rating is not available merely on an invoice basis; it is substantiated only by customs clearance records and external document flow.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) reflecting KCS export clearance acceptance for the consignment of shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire
Ocean or air Bill of Lading evidencing export from a Korean customs port to the foreign buyer's destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export contract issued by the Korean LLC to the overseas scrap purchaser

Foreign exchange bank settlement confirmation, SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice, documentary credit negotiation advice, or outward collection documentary credit documents showing receipt by the domicile foreign-exchange bank of the export proceeds
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation issued in Korea by a licensed foreign-exchange bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and KCS conduct joint risk-based audits against the electronic tax-invoice ledger, UNIPASS export declarations, sea/air waybills, scrap-metal purchase certificates, and the Foreign Exchange Information Database. If a zero-rated export is found to be unsubstantiated, overstated, not physically cleared, or if foreign currency is not repatriated within the 180-day statutory collection period without an approved extension, the supply is reclassified as taxable in the original period. The NTS will assess the 10% VAT underpaid together with additional tax and daily overdue interest, and can add further surcharges for misdeclaration. Fraudulently issued or altered export or tax documents trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the duty-fraud provisions of the Customs Act, and the retrospective reassessment period is extended to ten years from the relevant payment period for fraudulent or misrepresentative export transactions. The claim to refund of input VAT on the purchased scrap raw material is concurrently clawed back when the corresponding export is recharacterized as taxable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) serving as the senior foreign exchange control authority under South Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and subordinate regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized current-account convertibility regime for the Korean won. Payments and transfers for trade, dividends, royalties, and ordinary business expenses can generally be routed through domestic foreign exchange banks without prior administrative approval; however, the supporting underlying transaction must be reported and documented under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital-account operations, by contrast, require prior declaration or registration with a designated foreign exchange bank, the MOEF, or the BOK depending on the type of transaction, and portfolio investment and external borrowing may be subject to ceilings, reporting thresholds, and prudential measures. Export earnings are not subject to a blanket surrender order in ordinary practice; exporters may hold eligible foreign exchange in domestic foreign currency accounts. The practical hurdles to profit remittance are concentrated in the underlying evidence requirements: the remitting company must present tax clearance, audited financial statements, and a board resolution or equivalent proof of dividend/earnings distribution, while any inbound foreign investment must have been reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to ensure the corresponding foreign exchange bank can release the outward remittance. For a non-resident-owned Korean LLC engaged in scrap copper wire trading, the major convertibility constraint is therefore not daily currency availability, but the need to document every beneficial transaction in a manner that satisfies both Korean AML/KYC expectations and Foreign Exchange Information System reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For export trade receipts, the standard collection period is 180 calendar days from the date of export declaration unless an extension is obtained from a designated foreign exchange bank. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio for ordinary export proceeds: the Korean won is not required to be repurchased with all export proceeds, and a trader may keep foreign currency in a licensed onshore foreign currency account. However, export proceeds must be settled through and reported to the domestic foreign exchange bank, and any conversion to Korean won is executed at the prevailing market rate. Non-compliant settlement or delaying beyond the 180-day collection period may trigger regulatory penalties and loss of trade financing support.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account plus Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with export proceeds collection in foreign currency
Capital Escrow Account with Trade Settlement Rubric
Basic Operational Currency Account and Documentary LC Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not a compliant substitute for licensed Korean banks. South Korea restricts money exchange and receipt of funds to entities authorized under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. A foreign EMI without a Korean financial business license cannot open a domestic won account, cannot transmit Korean won on behalf of the LLC, and cannot execute the statutory reporting to the Foreign Exchange Information System. At best, an offshore EMI could be used as a non-budgetary information rail for foreign-currency side pockets, but it must not act as the treasury clearing counterparty for Korean-domiciled profit distributions or trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is required. For a Korean LLC with non-resident directors, the bank will require at least one natural-person director, UBO, or formally appointed authorised signatory to appear at a Korean domestic branch for identification. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the initial corporate account as it does not satisfy the Real Name Financial Transactions Act's face-to-face identification expectations or the Financial Action Task Force-style AML risk controls applied by compliance committees. If a representative is used, the power of attorney must be notarised and apostilled/legalised, and the representative's passport and alien registration certificate must be produced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain with nested foreign LLCs hiding the natural-person owners of the scrap copper trading entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crystalized corporate diagram showing every intermediate shareholder, individual passports of every UBO holding 25% or more, jurisdiction-specific registry extracts issued within the last 90 days, public accounting or law firm confirmation, and a signed UBO declaration explaining the source of wealth for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Scrap metal commodity typology: risk of trade-based money laundering through over/under-invoicing, artificially inflated copper quality, or commingled scrap originating from sanctioned or undocumented suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete purchase contract chain from original scrap generator to exporter, customs export declarations with HS 7404 valuation, weight and quality certificates from an independent surveyor such as SGS or Intertek, supplier tax invoices, transport documents including bill of lading and CMR inland receipts, and a commodity price assessment showing the invoice price within a defensible tolerance of London Metal Exchange copper reference prices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Utility of the account as a pass-through hub: frequent third-party inbound wire bonuses, split collections from non-counterparty payors, or rapid outgoing transfers without underlying commodity movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer onboarding exhibiting a standard sales-back-to-back purchase model, evidence of actual physical storage or logistics contracts, warehouse receipts with deliverable weight, inventory ageing reports, commercial invoices and corresponding SWIFT MT103 fields where the reason for payment references an underlying import/export transaction, and a treasury policy stating that no third-party payments are accepted without written consent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Environmental and licensing mismatch: export of shredded recycled copper wire without Korea's appropriate waste trade and metal recycling permits, thereby exposing the bank to regulatory concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 4669 trade-specific business licenses, Korean Ministry of Environment waste exporter registration certificate or the applicable non-hazardous metal scrap exemption, valid consignee permits in the destination jurisdiction, an environmental compliance policy, and annual audited statements showing the physical-wastage and recycling flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a non-resident equity injection into KR_YUHANGHOESA, the foreign investor files a foreign investment report at a designated Korean foreign exchange bank or KOTRA before remittance. Funds are wired via SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary bank details of the Korean bank branch and cleared into a Capital Escrow Account. The applicable foreign exchange purpose code should identify foreign direct investment and the equity contribution is verified by a certified Korean public accountant or bank confirmation before issuance or updating of the Foreign Investment Certificate. Any foreign currency loan receivable or sale-side prepayment used as capital must be separately reported and cannot be commingled with operating receipts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for recycled copper scrap merchandise should clear through SWIFT MT103 when payment is by telegraphic transfer, with full underlying contract and invoice references. For larger cross-border trade, the preferred rail is a commercial irrevocable letter of credit issued by a Korean bank and advised/confirmed by the seller's bank, with documents ideally including beneficiary certificate, port surveyor report, bill of lading, and packing list. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are workable for stable counterparties and provide a cheaper uncleared payment route, but they remain subject to Korean bank scrutiny and customs reporting. All disbursements must be within the reported business scope and flagged with the relevant import declaration or trade-finance code when a Korean won-foreign currency conversion is involved.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contracts (FX forwards) with actual trade or investment underlyings, booked through a Korean foreign exchange bank for hedging export receivables or import payables in USD/EUR or other fully convertible currencies
Direct cross-currency swaps between Korean won and USD tied to foreign direct investment or trade financing facilities, subject to the bank's maturity and tenors framework
OTC currency options and interest rate swaps to hedge currency and funding risk for the LLC's working capital, with real position documentation

Forbidden/speculative non-deliverable forward strategies involving Korean won referenced against offshore NDF markets are not permissible for a resident trading entity; any hedge must have a genuine underlying exposure and be reported to the designated bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax electronic filing system); the corporate component of local income tax is paid concurrently through the competent local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return must be filed between 1 March and 31 March of the following year; for other fiscal year ends, within three months after the fiscal year-end. One month extension is available by prior application.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-reporting penalties range from 10 percent to 40 percent of the underpaid tax depending on willfulness; statutory late-payment interest of approximately 3.5 percent per annum accrues daily; prolonged failure to file and pay may trigger tax seizure, cancellation of business registration, and a court-ordered dissolution or strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Si, Gun, or Gu local government, submitted simultaneously with the National Tax Service corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the corporate income tax return: by 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end, or within three months after any other fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment of local income tax attracts an additional tax of 10 percent to 40 percent and daily late-payment interest; continuing delinquency may result in compulsory collection, business closure, and director or member liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (DART), with a copy submitted as part of the annual corporate tax return package where external audit is legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory auditor must complete and file the audit report so that the audited financial statements are finalized and submitted with the annual corporate tax return by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end for standard 31 December fiscal years.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo a mandatory external audit or late filing of the audit report renders the annual tax filing defective and subjects the company and responsible directors to administrative fines under the External Audit Act; the National Tax Service may also impose non-filing penalties on the corporate return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Members' General Meeting and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Yuhan Hoesa corporate records maintained at the registered office; certified resolutions retained for statutory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general meeting of members must be held within three months from the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December balance-sheet date this means by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default in holding the annual members' meeting or failure to approve and keep the financial statements violates the Commercial Act and may expose executive managers to administrative fines up to KRW 10 million; repeated non-compliance may support involuntary dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Shareholding Transfer Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service and Financial Intelligence Unit compliance records; internal statutory registers retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The beneficial owner list must be confirmed as at the fiscal year-end and retained with the corporate tax file by 31 March; any transfer of quota interests or any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be recorded and reported within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted beneficial ownership information may result in anti-money laundering penalties under the Specific Financial Transaction Information Act, including imprisonment up to three years and fines up to KRW 50 million; tax records may also be treated as false declarations, triggering additional tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register, Statutory Books, and Dormant-Entity Strike-off Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent district court commercial registry; statutory books inspectable by tax and AML authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory registers and commercial books must be continuously maintained through the fiscal year and completed no later than the annual closing date of 31 December, with supporting member confirmation by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company that files no corporate or value-added tax returns for at least one year and shows no business activity may have its business registration canceled by the tax authority and may be struck off or judicially dissolved under the Commercial Act; failure to preserve statutory books may attract fines for directors and executive managers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to procure an independent certified CPA audit if, at the applicable fiscal year-end, it meets any of the following criteria: total assets of KRW 12 billion or more; total assets of KRW 7 billion or more together with annual revenue of KRW 100 billion or more; total assets of KRW 7 billion or more together with an average workforce of 500 or more employees. Mandatory audit is also required irrespective of the size thresholds if the entity is a listed or securities-reporting issuer, a financial company, an insurance company, an investment business entity, a mutual savings bank, or another statutorily designated regulated enterprise. The thresholds are determined on the basis of the standalone and, where applicable, consolidated financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements of audited Korean enterprises must be prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards where mandatory, or Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for non-public small and medium enterprises that are not required to adopt K-IFRS. The same accounting framework must be used for the statutory books, external audit report, and corporate income tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea applies a tax-transparency and AML-based beneficial ownership confirmation regime rather than maintaining a publicly searchable UBO register. The Yuhan Hoesa must identify the ultimate individual owner controlling or economically benefiting from the company's equity quota, confirm that ownership as at the fiscal year-end, and preserve a written UBO confirmation to be presented to the National Tax Service or Financial Intelligence Unit on request. Any change in quota ownership or beneficial ownership must be recorded in the statutory books and reported to the competent authority within 30 days of the transfer. The annual UBO confirmation is made in conjunction with the corporate tax return due by 31 March. The completed statutory registers and books must remain at the registered office and be made available for supervised inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Quota Interests
Register of Directors and Executive Managers
Register of Charges, Mortgages, and Secured Liabilities
Minute Book of Executive Management Decisions
Commercial Ledger and Annual Closing Books

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 3,200 per annum for registered office, corporate secretarial maintenance, statutory register administration, and compliance calendar management in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 to USD 22,000 per annum for a fully independent certified CPA audit, depending on transaction volume, physical scrap copper inventories, and cross-border documentary credit and SWIFT payment flows

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% (including 10% local surtax on the national corporate income tax) for the top bracket; graduated rates range from 10% to 25% for the national tax before surtax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays, preferential free-zone incentives, or patent box / R&D deduction regimes: South Korea provides a Patent Box-style regime (excess R&D expenditure tax credit; up to 40% of qualifying IP income can be excluded via the 'tax law special provisions for technology transfer' under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, Article 23), a 5-year corporate tax holiday for eligible free-trade-zone logistics and manufacturing entities (subject to zone designation and job creation), and a 2% preferential tax rate for certain foreign-invested high-tech enterprises in free economic zones under the Special Acts on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones. A Yuhan Hoesa engaged solely in cross-border recycled scrap copper wire trading may not easily qualify for R&D or patent box benefits unless it develops proprietary sorting or metallurgical recovery technology.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form 1 (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) filed via HomeTax electronic filing system (www.hometax.go.kr); supplementary schedules include Form 3 (Adjustment of Taxable Income) and Form 15 (Withholding Tax on Foreign Entities)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is three months after the end of the fiscal year-end (March 31 for a December 31 year-end); interim tax payment (semi-annual) is due within 2 months of the end of the first six-month half-year period (by August 31 for calendar-year entities). The annual return must be accompanied by audited financial statements when total assets exceed KRW 12 billion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identifier assigned by the Korean National Tax Service (NTS) to the Yuhan Hoesa; must match the Corporate Registry certificate and the trade name of the LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa, disclose the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) foreign parent and ensure the Foreign Investment Registration (FIRC) number is cross-referenced. Non-resident shareholders must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) at the time of filing to support any treaty-based reductions in paper dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the entity and the name, resident registration number, or foreign passport number of the statutory representative (the 'subject person' under assessment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the representative is a non-resident director, enter the Alien Registration Number. This person becomes the primary addressee of statutory assessment notices and demand letters. A foreign director's personal liability may be invoked for willful failure to pay withheld taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Begin and end dates of the fiscal year. All international transactions denominated in foreign currency must be converted to KRW using the base rate on the last day of the fiscal year (or an approved forward rate for actual settlements).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use spot rates from the NTS official exchange rate table. Do not use a blended migration average unless specifically authorized. Mismatches between the Korean filing period and the parent's fiscal year are common and must be reconciled in Schedule of Intercompany Transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (수입금액 및 매출총이익 / Gross Revenue and Gross Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales of recycled scrap copper wire, including both export shipments and any domestic sales. Gross profit is computed as total revenue minus cost of goods sold. Under the OECD transfer pricing principle, all intercompany sales must be adjusted to the arm's length price.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa acts as a 'commissionaire' purchasing scrap copper wire from local Korean suppliers and reselling to a related overseas buyer, only the commission or service fee embedded in the transaction may be recognized as income if an advanced pricing arrangement (APA) or a central procurement agreement is in place. The full gross margin must be substantiated by a Functional and Economic Analysis (FEA).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (각종 손금 및 접대비 / Deductible Expenses and Entertainment Expense Limits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares all business expenses, including purchase of scrap metal, transportation, freight, customs duties, and warehousing costs. Expense deductibility thresholds for entertainment (접대비) apply: KRW 12 million base plus 0.2% of revenue, with such expenses including the VAT gross-up and non-business meals being partially non-deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where payments are made to a non-resident service provider (e.g., a foreign inspection agency), the payor must withhold 20% corporate income tax on services rendered unless a zero-rate treaty provision applies. Under-documented payments to foreign related parties are a red flag for transfer pricing recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (과세표준 및 세액계산 / Taxable Income and Tax Computation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: After adjusting Book Income by permanent and temporary differences, the taxable base attracts national corporate income tax: 10% on income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 22% on income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; 25% on income exceeding KRW 300 billion. A 10% local surtax is then imposed on the national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident subsidiaries must also report 'deemed dividends' and minimum distributions if any recharacterization under the Korean thin capitalization rules (CAP art. 28) applies. Compute the statutory DTA relief separately: the Korean branch/LLC remittance tax is 20% for profits remitted to a foreign head office, unless the DTA limits it; but Korea does not impose a remittance tax on a subsidiary dividend payment — instead, a 20% domestic dividend withholding tax applies, subject to treaty reduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Comprehensive summary of late filing penalties, daily surcharges, and criminal fraud thresholds: Late filing penalty amounts to 0.5% of unpaid tax per day for up to 45 days (i.e., 20% maximum), plus an additional 0.6% per 1% of understatement on intentional omission (up to 40% gross negligence penalty). Failure to file a return entirely triggers a 20% flat penalty on the unpaid tax. Failure to issue or obtain an invoice under the VAT law results in a penalty of 2% of the invoice amount. Withholding tax failure on dividend interest, or royalty payments to a non-resident triggers a 20% surcharge plus an additional 1% per day up to 30% of the withheld amount. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (조세범처벌법) for willful understatement exceeding KRW 500 million may result in imprisonment up to five years or a fine of up to three times the evaded tax. Directors who instruct or authorize such evasion are personally jointly liable for the penalty and can be criminally prosecuted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (domestic rate under the Corporate Income Tax Act, Article 98), imposed on the gross dividend outbound to a non-resident shareholder; an additional 2% local income tax surcharge is added, resulting in an effective withholding burden of 20.4% (the local surcharge on withholding is subject to the Foreign Tax Credit in the parent's home jurisdiction).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Mandatory administrative process to invoke DTA relief, including Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial ownership substantiation: To claim a reduced rate (for example, 5% portfolio dividend / 10% significant holding dividend, or 10% interest/royalty depending on the treaty), the non-resident shareholder must submit: (i) a written 'Application for Non-Taxation or Exemption of Withholding Tax on Foreign-Income Recipients' (서면 제출) to the Korean payer or the NTS before the payment date; (ii) the original Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign revenue authority within one year, bearing an apostille or consular legalization; (iii) proof of beneficial ownership (BO) — the applicant must own the shares in its own name for imperative no less than 365 days if the DTA includes a limitation-on-benefits (LOB) clause, and must not be a pass-through, hybrid, or conduit merely channeling the dividend to a third-country resident; (iv) a statement of direct ownership percentage and the identity of all ultimate shareholders; (v) where treaty relief is not accepted, the withholding tax must be paid and a refund suit via the Board of Audit or administrative litigation can be filed. Failure to secure the TRC and BO declaration before the payment date converts the low treaty rate into the full 20.4% statutory withholding, with refund possible only through the non-resident 'collective advance agreement' procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory and treaty rates for intellectual property royalties and intercompany debt interest: Statutory interest withholding rate is 20% (plus 2% local surtax for a total of 20.4%). Statutory royalty withholding on patent, know-how, trademark and management fees is also 20% (plus 2% local surtax, i.e., 20.4%) — but Korean tax law deem it as dividend income if the royalty is paid to a controlling non-resident shareholder (30% or more ownership) under Article 93-10, unless the DTA overrides. Under the OECD Model treaty, Korean DTA rates typically reduce interest to 10% (5% for financial institutions in some treaties) and royalties to 10% (including payments for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment in historic treaties; but from 2020 Korean tables have largely aligned with the OECD Model eliminating equipment rental royalties). Korea's DTA with the US reduces dividends to 10% (15% for portfolio, 25% for certain US REITs), interest to 10%, royalties to 10%. The DTA relief procedure for interest and royalties is identical to dividend — a TRC, a beneficial ownership certificate, and evidence of actual economic use of the financed capital or IP must be presented at the time of payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Statutory intercompany transaction threshold triggering mandatory Local File / Master File preparation: In South Korea, the Financial Year transaction threshold for mandatory transfer pricing documentation is KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.5 million) for intercompany sales of goods and KRW 5 billion (approx. USD 3.75 million) for intercompany service, loan, and royalty transactions. However, even below these thresholds, a fabricated report should be prepared for internal risk management. The Local File (including the 'Transaction Detail Statement' — 극히 요약된 거래명세서) must be submitted to the NTS within 45 days of year-end if the threshold is met. A Master File (or 'Global Business and Financial Data') must be filed if the consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and the Korean entity has cross-border related-party transactions above the product/service thresholds.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicability of Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA): Although South Korea does not implement the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, the Korean Tax Adjustment Act (International Tax Coordination Act) imposes the substance-over-form doctrine and a 'preparation of economic substance documentation' requirement. Under Article 4 (Principle of Substantiality), the NTS may recharacterize a transaction that has no business purpose. For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa acting as an intermediary in scrap copper wire trading, the CJGA (Core Income-Generating Activities) must be performed in Korea: local directors must conduct actual negotiation, quality inspection, and logistics management. The presence of a mere letterbox office or offshore agglomeration of functions in a low-tax country will trigger a transfer pricing adjustment and treaty abuse denial under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) of the BEPS MLI. The entity should maintain board meeting minutes, transportation contracts, inspection certificates, and a functional cost analysis proving that freight risk, inventory risk, and credit risk are truly borne and managed by the Korean entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illicit Commercial Trade / Export Misdeclaration (shipping or customs fraud)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC knowingly under-declares the value, weight, or grade of recycled scrap copper wire in the export customs declaration, or misclassifies non-ferrous scrap under a heading with VAT exemption or lower tariff, in order to evade export VAT or customs duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Korean Customs Act (관세법) Article 270 and the Foreign Trade Act (대외무역법) Article 3-5, false declaration triggers a penalty of up to 10 times the evaded customs duty (minimum KRW 100 million), plus an administrative fine for customs entry. Additionally, the VAT Act Article 67 imposes a 2% invoice penalty and an additional evasion penalty of up to 40% of the evaded VAT. The exporter may be suspended from trading privileges for up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: The deputy director and statutory representative may be deemed jointly and severally liable for the unpaid export duties and penalties under the Customs Act Article 277-2 if they materially participated in the misdeclaration. Civil asset restitution of all undeclared profits, a travel ban (blacklisting) is automatically issued for unpaid customs dues exceeding KRW 5 million, and criminal imprisonment up to 5 years under Article 270 can be imposed. Additionally, the director's personal tax information will be published by the NTS Custom Office in annual defaulters' lists.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (anti-abuse and tax evasion)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC is classified as a shell or conduit because it has no local office, no employees, and no substantive purchase/sale function, but merely passes invoices between a foreign parent and foreign brokers to shift profits out of Korea via over-invoicing of purchase and under-invoicing of sales, while the revenue is later extracted as 'interest' on an artificial loan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Tax Coordination Act (국제조세조정에관한법률) Article 5 permits the NTS to recharacterize the income of a no-substance Korean entity as business income attributable to a permanent establishment of the foreign parent, with a 20% corporate income tax plus 20.4% withholding on 'deemed dividend' remittance. Article 6 of the same law disallows excessive interest deduction for thin capitalization if the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds 3:1 (6:1 for bank loans). The total penalty can reach up to 60% of the understated corporate liability, and the entity may be deregistered from the corporate register under the Commercial Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Korean courts frequently apply the 'actual decision-maker' doctrine under Article 401 of the Commercial Act: a director who knowingly authorized or facilitated the shell arrangement is personally liable to the entity and to the NTS for the amount of tax evaded plus interest. A criminal verdict under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 (willful evasion exceeding KRW 100 million) carries imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to triple the evaded tax. The director is also subject to blacklisting by the National Tax Service, which blocks overseas travel for up to one year, and revocation of the Foreign Investment Registration Status, thereby eliminating future visa permissions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Anti-Money Laundering Infraction (trade-based money laundering through phantom scrap shipments)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company issues false invoices for recycled copper wire that is never actually delivered, or receives wire transfers from a prohibited-source bank in a sanctioned jurisdiction while falsely declaring the bills of lading and certificates of origin, thereby using the recycled-scrap business as a laundering channel for illegal funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Transactions Reports Act (특정금융거래정보의보고및이용에관한법률) and the Crime Proceeds Concealment Regulation, culpable parties may be fined up to three times the laundered amount (minimum KRW 100 million); the Korea Customs Service imposes a penalty of KRW 50 million up to KRW 300 million for unregulated cross-border currency and trade-based laundering; the export license for recycled scrap copper is revocable permanently, and the company may be subject to a mandatory freezing order and asset seizure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Prior to the AML amendment, the director of a corporate vessel is automatically deemed criminally liable under Article 7 of the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment (신용정보의 이용 및 보호에 관한 법률). The court may impose civil asset forfeiture of the laundered sum, a travel ban and passport confiscation, and imprisonment of up to 7 years for intentional money laundering. Directors also face disqualification from serving as a director of any regulated financial or trading company for up to 10 years; the NTS will void any corporation tax benefit, and the Korean FIU will share the director's personal data with the global Egmont Group, leading to systemic banking de-risking in every OECD jurisdiction.
